ms.report:
Proof of Achievement for Milestone 1: Comprehensive Library Enhancement
We are excited to present the Proof of Achievement for Milestone 1, "Comprehensive Library Enhancement." During the course of this project, we have rebranded our library to Argus, a .NET Indexing Library. This milestone has been successfully completed, fulfilling all the specified Outputs, Acceptance Criteria, and Evidence of Milestone Completion.
Project Rebranding:
・Previous Name: Cardano.Sync
・New Name: Argus - A .NET Indexing Library

The rebranding reflects our commitment to providing a more comprehensive and versatile indexing solution for the Cardano blockchain within the .NET ecosystem.
Milestone Outputs:
We have significantly enhanced the functionality of Argus, making it more versatile and robust. We have implemented everything we promised and even more, providing developers with extensive tools to interact with the Cardano blockchain.
Exposure of Complete CDDL Equivalent Fields/Data:
・We have fully exposed all CDDL equivalent fields and data structures, enabling comprehensive access to blockchain details. This includes blocks, transactions, inputs, UTXOs, certificates, datum, script references, withdrawals, metadata, minting information, and additional data elements that enhance the developer experience.

Implementation of General and Use-case Specific Reducers:
・Beyond the initial scope, we have implemented a suite of general reducers and common use-case dApp reducers. These tools simplify data processing and enable developers to build more efficient and powerful applications.
・Please note: A token Subject in Cardano generally means (PolicyId + AssetName) and hence the JpgPriceByAssetReducer was renamed to JpgPriceBySubjectReducer, the name has changed but logically they function the same. It can be found here.
・Please note: UtxoByAddressReducer, TransactionInputsReducer and TransactionOutputsReducer have been merged into one effiecient reducer (It can be found here).

Website: https://docs.saib.dev/

 - Practical implementation patterns for common use cases
